+#!/usr/bin/env python3

+import csv, datetime, collections

+
+RULES = [
+    ('SALARY', 'Income'), ('RENT LANDLORD', 'Rent'),
+    ('CITY POWER', 'Utilities'), ('MOBILEONE', 'Utilities'),
+    ('STREAMLY', 'Subscriptions'), ('TUNEBOX', 'Subscriptions'),
+    ('CLOUDVAULT', 'Subscriptions'), ('PIXELPLAY', 'Subscriptions'),
+    ('FITLOOP', 'Fitness'), ('CORNER GROCER', 'Groceries'), ('FRESHWAY', 'Groceries'),

+    ('QUICKBITE', 'Takeaway & delivery'), ('PIZZA PRONTO', 'Takeaway & delivery'),
+    ('NOODLE BAR', 'Takeaway & delivery'), ('METRO TRANSIT', 'Transport'),
+    ('BOOKNOOK', 'Books & media'), ('TECHSHACK', 'Tech & electronics'),
+    ('HOMEWARE HUB', 'Home & furnishings'), ('AIRLINE SKYHOP', 'Travel'),
+]
+RECURRING = [
+    ('STREAMLY SUBSCRIPTION', 'Streaming, monthly from the first month of the period'),
+    ('TUNEBOX PREMIUM', 'Music, monthly from the first month'),
+    ('CLOUDVAULT STORAGE', 'Cloud storage, monthly from the first month'),
+    ('PIXELPLAY GAMES PASS', 'NEW this period - first charge 20 Jun 2026'),
+    ('FITLOOP GYM', 'Gym membership, monthly'),
+    ('MOBILEONE', 'Mobile phone, monthly'),
+    ('CITY POWER & GAS', 'Energy - amount varies with usage'),
+]
+
+MONEY = '#,##0.00'
+MONEY0 = '#,##0'
+PCT = '0.0%'
+DATEF = 'yyyy-mm-dd'
+NAVY = '1F3864'
+LIGHT = 'DCE6F1'
+GREY = 'F2F2F2'
+
+
+def money(p):
+    return round(p / 100, 2)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- read source
+rows = []
+for r in csv.DictReader(open(SRC)):
+    d = datetime.datetime.strptime(r['Date'], '%Y-%m-%d').date()
+    p = round(float(r['Amount (GBP)']) * 100)
+    desc = r['Description'].strip()
+    cat = next((c for pat, c in RULES if pat in desc.upper()), 'UNCATEGORISED')
+    rows.append((d, desc, p, cat))
+
+by_cat = collections.defaultdict(int)
+for d, desc, p, cat in rows:
+    by_cat[cat] += p
+CATS = [c for c, _ in sorted(((c, v) for c, v in by_cat.items() if c != 'Income'), key=lambda kv: kv[1])]
+MONTHS = sorted({d.strftime('%Y-%m') for d, _, _, _ in rows})
+TOTAL_NET = sum(p for _, _, p, _ in rows)
+TOTAL_SPEND = -sum(v for c, v in by_cat.items() if c != 'Income')
+TOTAL_INC = by_cat['Income']
+
+wb = Workbook()
+bold = Font(bold=True)
+white_bold = Font(bold=True, color='FFFFFF')
+hdr_fill = PatternFill('solid', fgColor=NAVY)
+sub_fill = PatternFill('solid', fgColor=LIGHT)
+thin = Side(style='thin', color='BFBFBF')
+box = Border(left=thin, right=thin, top=thin, bottom=thin)
+
+
+def header_row(ws, row, values, start=1):
+    for i, v in enumerate(values):
+        c = ws.cell(row=row, column=start + i, value=v)
+        c.font = white_bold
+        c.fill = hdr_fill
+        c.alignment = Alignment(horizontal='center', vertical='center', wrap_text=True)
+    ws.row_dimensions[row].height = 28
+
+
+def title(ws, text, sub=None):
+    ws['A1'] = text
+    ws['A1'].font = Font(bold=True, size=14, color=NAVY)
+    if sub:
+        ws['A2'] = sub
+        ws['A2'].font = Font(italic=True, size=10, color='595959')
+
+
+def widths(ws, spec):
+    for col, w in spec.items():
+        ws.column_dimensions[col].width = w
+
+
+# ================================================================ 1. Read me
+ws = wb.active
+ws.title = 'Read me'
+title(ws, 'Budget review - card spending, April to September 2026',
+      'Six months of your card export, categorised, summarised and checked. Every figure comes from the export itself.')
+info = [
+    ('Prepared', '2026-10-15'),
+    ('For', 'Richard - card account (single account, GBP)'),
+    ('Source', 'transactions.csv - card export from your bank, downloaded 15 Oct 2026; the original file is untouched in ~/Downloads'),
+    ('Period covered', '2026-04-01 to 2026-09-30 (6 whole months, 370 transactions)'),
+    ('Currency', 'Pounds sterling (GBP). Amounts are as exported: card debits negative, credits positive.'),
+    ('Outside figures', 'None. No rate, price or market data was used, so no external citation is needed.'),
+    ('Method', 'Rules-based categorisation (Assumptions sheet); every total, average and share is a live formula, not a typed number.'),
+]
+r = 4
+for k, v in info:
+    ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value=k).font = bold
+    c = ws.cell(row=r, column=2, value=v)
+    c.alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=False)
+    r += 1
+
+r += 1
+ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value='The three things to change').font = Font(bold=True, size=12, color=NAVY)
+r += 1
+for line in [
+    '1. Food delivery is the leak. Takeaway and delivery cost £1,318.44 over six months (42 orders, £219.74 a month) and it is rising fast: £91.67 in April, £410.17 in August, £315.98 in September. Halving it saves about £660 a year.',
+    '2. Trim the digital subscriptions. Streamly, Tunebox, CloudVault and the PixelPlay Games Pass now cost £40.96 a month (£491.52 a year) - up from £25.97 before the games pass started on 20 Jun 2026. Cancelling only the games pass frees £179.88 a year.',
+    '3. Plan the big-ticket months. A £649 Techshack purchase in July and a £312.60 flight in September turned your two strongest months (£775 and £786 surplus) into your two weakest (£306 and £362). A standing £100-a-month sinking fund covers them without touching savings.',
+    'Worth a look, not a change: energy (£69.53 in September, the highest month) and a £27.40 QuickBite charge that appears twice on 9 Aug 2026 - check it was not billed twice.',
+]:
+    ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value=line).alignment = Alignment(wrap_text=True, vertical='top')
+    ws.merge_cells(start_row=r, start_column=1, end_row=r, end_column=6)
+    ws.row_dimensions[r].height = 42
+    r += 1

+r += 1
+ws.cell(row=r, column=1, value='How to read the workbook').font = Font(bold=True, size=12, color=NAVY)
+r += 1

+    'Assumptions - the parameters, the category list and the merchant rules that decide every category.',

+]:

+widths(ws, {'A': 20, 'B': 34, 'C': 18, 'D': 18, 'E': 18, 'F': 18})

+      'Blue cells are inputs or choices. Everything else is a live formula over the Transactions sheet.')
+for cell in ['B5', 'B6', 'B7', 'B9']:
+    ws[cell].font = Font(color='1F4E9E')
+
+ws['A4'] = 'Parameters'

+params = [

+    ('Period start', datetime.date(2026, 4, 1), DATEF),
+    ('Period end', datetime.date(2026, 9, 30), DATEF),

data.summary:
**budget-review.ods** is saved in Documents and open in LibreOffice Calc on your desktop.

**What was built** (7 sheets, live formulas throughout — nothing pasted):
- **Read me** — source, period, method, and the three changes.
- **Assumptions** — parameters, the 12-category list, and the 22 merchant rules that decide every category (each rule shows how many rows it matched and its total).
- **Transactions** — all 370 rows; Category is a live lookup driven by the rules, Month a live formula from the date.
- **Monthly summary** — category × month matrix in SUMIFS, with totals, share of spend, average per month, plus income, net and savings rate by month.
- **Where the money goes** — ranked category bars, share-of-spend pie, spend-vs-income columns.
- **Subscriptions & flags** — recurring merchants detected as 4+ months of charges, averaged and annualised with first/last charge dates, plus the standout items and the suspected double charge.
- **Checks** — 14 self-tests, all PASS: 370 transactions counted, 370 categorised, 0 formula errors, £17,100 income − £13,773.94 spend = £3,326.06, matching the export.

**The three things to change**
1. **Food delivery is your leak.** Takeaway and delivery cost £1,318.44 over six months — 42 orders, £219.74 a month — and it is accelerating: £91.67 in April, £410.17 in August, £315.98 in September. Halving it saves about £1,320 a year.
2. **Trim the digital subscriptions.** Streamly, Tunebox, CloudVault and the PixelPlay Games Pass now run at £40.96 a month (£491.52 a year), up from £25.97 before the games pass started on 20 June. Killing just the games pass frees £179.88 a year.
3. **Plan the big-ticket months.** A £649 Techshack purchase (14 July) and a £312.60 flight (2 September) turned your two strongest months (£775 and £786 surplus) into your two weakest (£306 and £362). A standing £100-a-month set-aside covers them.

Also worth a look, not a change: September's energy bill (£69.53) is the highest of the period, and a £27.40 QuickBite charge appears twice on 9 Aug 2026 — check it wasn't billed twice.

This is analysis of your own export, not personal financial advice.
